Nvidia has hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to lead its CEO search following Jensen Huang's resignation, according to The Wall Street Journal.

$NVDA  - NVIDIA STOPS DISCLOSING SINGAPORE SALES AS REVENUE SURGES TO $104 BILLION

Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore-linked revenue after changing its geographic reporting methodology from customer billing addresses to headquarters locations, according to the Financial Times.

Its Singapore subsidiary booked $104 billion in external revenue in 2025, up 72%, representing nearly half of Nvidia's global sales.

The disclosure change comes amid U.S. investigations into Megaspeed, a major Singapore-based customer suspected of diverting advanced chips to China.

Nvidia says most Singapore-billed products were shipped elsewhere.

The shift raises transparency and export-control concerns, though it does not establish wrongdoing.

posts.author: The Kobeissi Letter
posts.text:
It's officially Nvidia's earnings day.

Today's earnings report and call will likely be the most watched earnings event in history.

We are watching two key things:

1. Do executives show any willingness to reinstate Jensen Huang

2. What has CHANGED from a business perspective

As of now, considering the information over the last 48 hours, we believe there is an <20% chance that Jensen returns.

Any indication that the probability is higher would be strongly bullish for the stock.

But, if not, then what has changed for Nvidia? With or without Jensen, this company remains one of the best businesses in the world.

We are looking to see if the company still expects revenue growth of 70%+ in FY2028, as management previously indicated.

We also look for any changes to AI infrastructure spending, demand for Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips, and the company's relationships with its largest customers.

If the fundamental outlook remains intact, then investors must ask: Does Jensen Huang's departure justify the -$750 billion in lost market cap?

We believe the market has already priced in a significant portion of the uncertainty surrounding Jensen's departure.

At the same time, the long-term AI infrastructure investment cycle remains intact, and Nvidia continues to sit at the center of it.

The burden is now on management to demonstrate that the business can continue executing at the same level without Jensen Huang.

More to come after earnings.

posts.author: Wall St Engine
posts.text:
ANTHROPIC EXPECTS TO PRICE ITS IPO ABOVE $80 PER SHARE: WSJ

The Claude maker originally targeted $70-$78 per share, but its advisers are now discussing a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion, up from roughly $1.33 trillion at the initial range.

Hedge funds have placed unusually large orders, with Altimeter founder Brad Gerstner saying his firm requested $5 billion worth of shares.

Existing investors, including Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures and Accel, also reportedly plan to increase their investments rather than sell down their stakes.

At the original price range, Anthropic planned to sell around $61 billion in IPO shares, alongside a separate $26 billion private placement backed by investors including Google and Nvidia. The company also plans to allocate up to 20% of the IPO to retail investors.

Final pricing is expected Wednesday, with trading set to begin Thursday on the Nasdaq under $ANT.
